claims.value: Toreno gives side A about 8,000 joined troops, including 600 cavalry, approaching Alcañiz.
claims.rationale: Opponent estimate of joined divisions; not a French own muster. English rendering (ours): "Together the two [divisions] numbered about 8,000, of whom 600 were cavalry."

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 8,176 infantry and 481 cavalry after joining the Morella and Tortosa divisions.
claims.rationale: Joined field force; exact engaged subset remains unknown. English rendering (ours): "The Spanish general, after joining the Valencian Morella and Aragonese Tortosa divisions, counted 8,176 infantry and 481 cavalry."

claims.value: Suchet assigns Fabre the principal column against Las Horcas, within Suchet’s newly assumed chief command.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Fabre, at the head of the 114th and 1st Vistula, advanced in attack column against the hill defended by cannon and infantry."

claims.value: Toreno places the Spanish centre immediately under Blake and his second Lazan, Areizaga on the right and Roca on the left.
claims.rationale: The page names Areizaga and Roca for their sectors; no equal credit follows. English rendering (ours): "The centre was on the Capuchin height under the immediate orders of the chief and his second, Marquis Lazan."

claims.value: Suchet says the column unexpectedly met a recently completed broad cut at the hill foot.
claims.rationale: Continuation of the final line on p.18. This is the memoir’s explanation, not a measured causal effect. English rendering (ours): "A broad cut, recently completed, unexpectedly stopped the column."
